author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A Bronx man has been charged with driving under the influence and reckless driving after a fiery Middletown crash killed a child younger than 3 and seriously injured another passenger, police said. The new charges are a material update to the crash investigation first reported Wednesday.

Police identified the driver as 32-year-old Jerry Bonilla. He faces counts including DUI resulting in death, DUI resulting in serious bodily injury, driving to endanger resulting in death and driving to endanger resulting in injury. At a Thursday arraignment, a judge set surety bail at $500,000 and ordered Bonilla held at the Adult Correctional Institutions.

Authorities said Portsmouth police attempted to stop the sedan at about 1:20 a.m. on West Main Road near Mill Lane after recording it at 58 mph in a 45-mph zone. Police said the vehicle accelerated to roughly 80 to 90 mph. The Portsmouth officer ended the attempted stop near Union Street and alerted Middletown police.

The sedan later struck a utility pole and stone wall near Linden Park and caught fire, investigators said. The child died and another occupant suffered serious injuries. The charges are allegations, and Bonilla is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. The crash remains under investigation.
dek: Police identified the driver in Wednesday’s West Main Road crash and filed felony DUI and reckless-driving charges after a child died and another passenger was seriously injured.
headline: Driver charged with fatal DUI after Middletown crash kills child
